name: Credential or PIN entry demanded in order to receive money
description: An authorising action — entering a UPI PIN, sharing an OTP, scanning a QR — is framed as necessary to RECEIVE a payment. Receiving money never requires authorisation; the action would send money out. This is a directional contradiction, not a keyword match.

source_references.quote: Always remember, you don't need a UPI PIN or OTP to receive money.

explanation.plain: You have been asked to enter a PIN, share a code, or scan a QR in order to RECEIVE money. Receiving money never needs any of these. Anything you approve here would send your money out, not bring money in.
explanation.technical: RECEIVE_FRAMING combined with a credential or payment-authorisation prompt, spanning payment-action and credential-action classes. CERT-In states the boundary categorically.
verification_steps: Open your UPI app directly. Incoming payments appear without any action from you.
If someone insists a PIN is needed to receive, that alone settles it.

provenance.notes: Originally cited to NPCI (SRC-005, SRC-018), both unreachable (G-02). Re-anchored to CERT-In, which is arguably a stronger basis: national CERT, categorical wording (RESEARCH-004 section 5). QR_SCAN_REQUEST was removed from the trigger set at validation: the linter flagged that RECEIVE_FRAMING + QR_SCAN_REQUEST spans a single evidence class, and on inspection the rule was also reaching past its own quotation — SRC-021's wording here concerns a UPI PIN or OTP, not QR. The 'scan QR to receive' pattern is TL-PAY-002's subject.
